sections.heading: How to Play
sections.content: Clash-A-Mana is a real-time card battle game. Deploy cards to the arena using mana, destroy the opponent's tower to win. Each card costs mana — manage your resources wisely.
list: Mana - The energy resource used to deploy cards. Regenerates over time.
Tower - Your base. If destroyed, you lose the match.
Arena - A three-route battlefield with a straight central lane, two longer outer lanes, and three capturable mana wells.
Cycle - Your deck of 8 cards cycles continuously during battle.

sections.heading: Rarity System
sections.content: Every entity in Clash-A-Mana has a rarity tier that reflects its power, scarcity, and role in the Stagnantia project. Higher rarity cards are harder to obtain but significantly more powerful.
list: Mundane - Common workers and basic constructs. Easy to deploy, reliable.
Familiar - Trained soldiers and tamed beasts. Good synergy potential.
Arcane - Mystic entities infused with portal energy. Unique abilities.
Relic - Ancient warriors of legend. High cost, high impact.
Ascendant - Evolved beings beyond normal classification.
Apex - The pinnacle of combat power. Extremely rare.
Emergent - Cards that gain new traits as they are used.
Ethereal - Beings that exist between dimensions. Unpredictable and devastating.

sections.heading: Sides
sections.content: Stagnantia is divided into two opposing sides, locked in perpetual conflict for the entertainment of the Crimson Crown. Every card wielder belongs to one side - but the true enemy is the system itself.
list: The Crimson Crown - The ruling elite who architect and profit from the conflict.
The Azure Core - The working class, forced into the arena as entertainment.

sections.heading: Win Conditions
sections.content: Destroy the enemy tower to win immediately. If both towers survive the five-minute match, two minutes of overtime always follow with doubled mana regeneration. After overtime, the surviving tower with more health wins; equal health is a draw.
list: Tower Destruction - Instantly win by destroying the opponent's tower.
Higher Health - If both towers survive overtime, the tower with more remaining health wins; equal health is a draw.
Overtime - Two extra minutes with doubled mana regeneration whenever both towers survive regulation.
Perfect Victory - Destroy tower without taking any damage yourself.

sections.heading: Card Stats
sections.content: Cards have 24 numerical stats. Distances use 1,000 source points per tile; Speed is measured in tiles per second.
list: Health - The total amount of life your card has. When it reaches zero, your character dies.
Shield - By default, 70% of incoming damage goes to shield while it lasts. Shield Depletion changes this split; unabsorbed damage reaches health.
Damage - The amount of harm dealt to an enemy per hit or action.
Attack Speed - The interval in seconds between hits. Lower values mean faster attacks.
Delay - Extra recovery time after the final hit of an attack sequence.
Mana - The mana cost of deploying the card.
Count - The number of units deployed by one card. This is separate from the number of hits per attack.
Range - The maximum distance from which your card attacks or uses abilities.
Speed - How fast your card moves across the game world.
D.P.S. - Damage per second. The average damage your card deals each second over time.
Critical Damage - The extra damage dealt when a critical hit occurs.
Critical Chance - The percentage chance for an attack to become a critical hit.
Life Steal - A mechanic where a portion of dealt damage restores your health.
Life Steal Chance - The probability that an attack triggers life steal.
Damage Reduction - A stat that lowers incoming damage before it affects health.
Dodge - A chance-based mechanic that avoids incoming attacks completely.
Vision - The distance at which a card can detect targets, limiting its attack acquisition.
Healing Bonus - Increases healing received.
Rejuvenation - Health recovered per second.
Fortification - Shield recovered over time.
Critical Resistance - Reduces the bonus portion of incoming critical damage.
Flexibility - Shortens the duration of finite negative status effects.
Shield Depletion - The percentage of incoming damage assigned to shield while it is available.
Life - The unit's lifetime in seconds, when a lifetime is specified.

sections.heading: Positive Status Effects
list: Heal: Restores a specific amount of health to an ally card over a set duration.
Untouchable: Grants an ally card complete immunity to all incoming damage for a limited time.
Immortal: Prevents an ally card from dying from damage for a set duration; damage cannot reduce their health below 1.
Predominance: Removes current negative status effects and grants immunity to new negative effects for a limited time.
Fearless: Grants damage reduction to an ally card when no other ally cards are nearby, or when surrounded by more than 5 enemy cards.
Taunt: Forces nearby enemy cards to focus their attacks exclusively on the casting ally card for a set duration.
Cleanse: Removes all current negative effects.
Berserk: Increases attack speed or attack damage when health falls below a threshold.
Invisibility: For a set duration and under certain conditions, an ally card cannot be targeted by any enemy card. The effect ends immediately if the card takes damage from spells or any other source.
Untargetable: For a set duration and under certain conditions, an ally card can neither be targeted nor damaged by enemy cards.
Reflection: For a set duration and under certain conditions, an ally card sends all damage of any type it receives from enemy cards back to the attacking card.

sections.heading: Negative Status Effects
list: Burn: Deals continuous damage to an enemy card over time, once every 1 second, and reduces their healing received by 20%.
Poison: Inflicts continuous damage to an enemy card over time, once every 0.75 seconds, and reduces their movement speed by 10%.
Slow: Decreases an enemy card's movement speed and attack speed by a specified percentage (minimum 10%).
Silence: Prevents an enemy card from activating or using any abilities.
Blind: Restricts an enemy card's vision and attack range by a specified percentage (minimum 12.5%).
Stat Reduction: Lowers the base stats of an enemy card by a specified amount.
Curse: Amplifies the damage an enemy card receives from all sources.
Stun: Immobilizes an enemy card for a set duration, preventing movement and attacks.
Bleeding: Deals continuous damage to an enemy card once every 1 second, equal to 1% of their maximum health, and completely blocks all forms of healing for the duration.
Misfortune: Reduces the target's accuracy. All basic attacks and abilities have a specified chance to miss (minimum 10%). Missed attacks deal no damage and apply no effects.
Imprisonment: For a set duration and under certain conditions, an enemy card can neither be targeted nor take damage, and it also cannot deal damage.
Root: For a set duration and under certain conditions, an enemy card cannot move.
Airborne: For a set duration and under certain conditions, enemy cards are launched into the air; during this time they can neither deal damage nor move.
Betrayal: For a set duration and under certain conditions, enemy cards deal damage to their own allies.
Knockback: Under certain conditions, enemy cards are pushed backwards.
Frozen: For a set duration and under certain conditions, enemy cards are frozen; for 3 seconds after thawing they are slowed by 25%.
